subject: simulateData with multiple groups and standardized option

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: simulateData with multiple groups and standardized option
parts:
Hello Yves,

I am using the development version of lavaan (0.5-16, downloaded a couple days ago) to generate a 2-group sample.  I'm not sure whether there is a bug, but I can't think of a reason why the script below would not work:

> popModel <- 'Y =~ .5*y1 + .6*y2 + .7*y3 + .8*y4'
> pop <- simulateData(popModel, model.type = "cfa", sample.nobs = c(8500, 1500),
+                     group.label = c("White", "Black"), std.lv = TRUE,
+                     standardized = TRUE, empirical = TRUE, seed = 3141593)
Error: trying to get slot "cov.x" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with no slots

When I remove the standardized argument (and specify residual variances manually), it runs fine:

popModel <- '
Y =~ .5*y1 + .6*y2 + .7*y3 + .8*y4
y1 ~~ .5*y1
y2 ~~ .5*y2
y3 ~~ .5*y3
y4 ~~ .5*y4
'

pop <- simulateData(popModel, model.type = "cfa", sample.nobs = c(8500, 1500),
                    group.label = c("White", "Black"), std.lv = TRUE,
                    empirical = TRUE, seed = 3141593)

Thanks for any insight,

Terry

parts:
Hi,

I am doing a simulation with planned missing design using lavaan and simsem package. The population model and the model without missing values worked fine. When the planned missing was included, I got the following error. Please give me some advice. Thank you very much.

popmodel <- "
#loadings
f1=~1*y1+start(0.5)*y2+start(0.5)*y3;
f2=~1*y4+start(0.5)*y5+start(0.5)*y6;
f3=~1*y7+start(0.5)*y8+start(0.5)*y9;
f4=~1*y10+start(0.5)*y11+start(0.5)*y12;
#variance
f1~~start(0.4)*f1;f2~~start(0.4)*f2;f3~~start(0.4)*f3;f4~~start(0.4)*f4;
y1~~start(0.3)*y1;y2~~start(0.3)*y2;y3~~start(0.3)*y3;y4~~start(0.3)*y4;
y5~~start(0.3)*y5;y6~~start(0.3)*y6;y7~~start(0.3)*y7;y8~~start(0.3)*y8;
y9~~start(0.3)*y9;y10~~start(0.3)*y10;y11~~start(0.3)*y11;y12~~start(0.3)*y12;
#covariance
f1~~start(0.3)*f2;f1~~start(0.3)*f3;f2~~start(0.3)*f3;
f1~~0*f4;f2~~0*f4;f3~~0*f4
"
analyzemodel1b <- "
#step2,simulate a simple cfa with a marker
f1=~NA*y1+y2+y3;f2=~NA*y4+y5+y6;f3=~NA*y7+y8+y9;f4=~NA*y1+y2+y3+y4+y5+y6+y7+y8+y9+y10+y11+y12;
f1~~f2;f1~~f3;f2~~f3;f1~~0*f4;f2~~0*f4;f3~~0*f4
"
output1b <- sim(1000, analyzemodel1b, n=500, generate=popmodel, lavaanfun = "cfa",std.lv=T)
itemgroups=list(setx=c(1,5,9),set1=c(2,6,10),set2=c(3,7,11),set3=c(4,8,12))
missmodel=miss(nforms=3,itmegroups=itemgroups)
> output2a=sim(1000, analyzemodel1b, n=500, generate=popmodel, lavaanfun = "cfa",miss=missmodel)
Error in cov(X[[g]], use = "pairwise") : 'x' is empty
In addition: Warning message:
In lav_data_full(data = data, group = group, group.label = group.label,  :
  lavaan WARNING: small number of observations (nobs < nvar)
  nobs = 0 nvar = 12

Looks like something went wrong with reading data.

Best regards,

ya

messages.subject: Re: simsem with planned missing
parts:
Hi Ya,

The issue is with the specification of the 3-forms missing data design. You need to specify the missing pattern as a separate object (using the miss function) and then pass that object to the miss argument in the sim function. Fro an example of this, see example 9 at simsem.org

Alex

  nobs = 0 nvar = 12

But I couldn't find anything beyond that.

Out of curiosity, I generated a single data set from Ya's population model, imposed the missing data pattern to verify it worked correctly, and analyzed it directly with cfa(), all of which works fine. 

## check whether one replication works
dat <- generate(model = popmodel, n = 500)
missdat <- impose(miss = missmodel, data.mat = dat)
out <- cfa(analyzemodel1b, missdat, std.lv = TRUE, missing = "fiml")
summary(out)
 
So I don't think it's a problem with lavaan, but I don't know the innards of simsem well enough to know where to chase down the elusive call to cov(X[[g]]).  It obviously seems like it's looking for a list of data for each group in X[[g]], but this is a one-group model.  Maybe simsem is missing some syntax to put the single-group data into a list so that something else works in lavaan, but I couldn't find where with debug().

Hope that helps a bit,

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899

On Wednesday, February 19, 2014 12:09:43 PM UTC-6, Yves Rosseel wrote:

The error happens in the function lavSampleStatsFromData() (in 0.5-16
dev renamed to lav_samplestats_from_data()). Perhaps debugging this
function might help.

It would seem that the data is empty.

Yves.

Thanks, Yves -- that helped me find the problem.

I think the problem is with the function simsem:::analyzeLavaan(), starting at line 120 in simsem's "analyze.R" file:

        # If the missing argument is not specified and data have NAs, the default is fiml.
        if(is.null(args$missing)) {
            missing <- "default"
            if (any(is.na(args$data))) {
                missing <- "fiml"
            }
        } else {
            missing <- args$missing
            args$missing <- NULL
        }

I'm not sure whether it was intentional to create an independent object called "missing", but I'm guessing the the lines in red font should be saving values "fiml" or "default" to args$missing instead, after checking the contents of the miss object to see what the user intended.  When running Ya's syntax with debug() turned on for simsem:::analyzeLavaan(), I manually add args$missing <- "fiml" to the args list, and the call to cfa() works fine after that.  The fact that the missing argument was missing in the call to cfa() meant that the value returned by lav_samplestats_from_data() was empty, since there were no complete observations in Ya's planned missing design.

Ya -- I'll push my suggested correction on github and email Sunthud about it.  I don't know when a new version would be released on CRAN, but simsem.org has instructions at the bottom of the page for installing a development version, whenever the change is accepted.

Terry

parts:
Yves,

I think I have found another "bug" (or minor oversight) that only happens when using "standardized = TRUE"

When calling simulateData() with standardized = TRUE, a copy of "lav" is created called "lav2" which is used in lavaan() to create the object "fit".  Two lines later, an error occurs when trying to create the object "ETA".  I think the problem is that the function computeVETA() is called while specifying "lavsamplestats" as NULL.  That seems to result in the following error:

mod.pop <- '
f1 =~ .7*y1 + .7*y2 + .7*y3
f2 =~ .7*y4 + .7*y5 + .7*y6
f1 ~~ .25*f2
'
dat <- simulateData(mod.pop, "cfa", standardized = TRUE, sample.nobs = 50)
Error: trying to get slot "cov.x" from an object of a basic class ("NULL") with no slots

From the for() loop in the computeVETA() function:
cov.x <- lav...@cov.x[[g]]
Since this is not conditional on a check for whether lavsamplestats is NULL, I was wondering whether this was a mistake.

When I specify error variances in the syntax and remove "standardized = TRUE", it runs without any error.

Thanks for your attention,

Terry
